mainEntity.name: How can I tell whether an AI-generated product idea is actually worth building?

acceptedAnswer.text: AI is usually most useful for producing a structured first draft, not for deciding what customers will buy. Run My AI Biz includes opportunity research, customer research, offer positioning, and product-planning examples to help owners investigate demand before investing heavily. Context: Research results can be incomplete, outdated, or overly confident, so they need independent checking. A polished draft does not prove that an audience has a problem or will pay for a solution. Key factors: - Look for repeated customer complaints, questions, workarounds, and buying behavior. - Compare competing offers and identify an underserved or clearer use case. - Ask prospective customers about priorities rather than presenting only an AI-generated concept. Practical guidance: Use AI to organize evidence and propose testable hypotheses, then validate the strongest hypothesis through conversations, preorders, surveys, or a small pilot. Keep assumptions clearly labeled in your planning documents.
acceptedAnswer.description: Treat an AI-generated idea as a hypothesis, not proof of demand. Use AI to organize customer research and competitor information, then validate the problem through conversations, a small pilot, preorder interest, or another measurable test before building extensively.
